basis: The dispatch table targets palette updates, scroll updates, and boss tile/palette setup handlers.
The selector word is loaded as a stage-configuration field and written by stage/camera setup code.
The only direct call is one step in the main gameplay rendering/effect chain, not the player state update.
The adjacent selector dispatches only palette fade and palette-update handlers.
It is called from the same gameplay graphics/effect chain as the primary dispatcher.
The payload is exactly 16 Mega Drive color words.
UI_InitializeSEGAScreen copies all 32 bytes into palette RAM immediately before loading sega_tiles.
The routine adds the Z-Leo velocity field to the horizontal scroll accumulator.
It neither reads nor writes palette memory.
Both outputs are derived from phase indices and the shared sine table.
The resulting fixed-point coordinates are written to the same camera target fields used by the Z-Leo ending sequence.
The routine checks the camera Y coordinate against 0x80 and 0x1C0.
Inside that range it copies camera coordinates to the target fields; outside it resets the target and a control flag.
It does not access palette memory.
The routine allocates sprite objects, assigns randomized positions and velocity, and selects sprite frame pointers.
It emits periodic sound effects after the particle loop.
It does not access palette memory.
The routine initializes one object slot from the active Z-Leo object's position and sprite attributes.
It plays a sound effect and performs no tilemap transfer.
The routine advances an accumulator and converts it to a bounded range.
It tail-calls the shared effect-pattern buffer filler and does not update entity coordinates.
The routine advances a second accumulator and tail-calls the effect-pattern buffer filler when the boss is active.
It does not access palette memory.
The routine mirrors the phase-B accumulator and pattern-fill behavior using a third state field.
It performs no object destruction or resource cleanup.
The routine writes zero across all 96 longwords of the effect-pattern buffer.
It neither allocates nor updates a projectile.
The routine fills a caller-selected range in the 96-entry effect-pattern buffer.
Its output is consumed by rendering transfer code rather than a projectile spawner.
The routine prepares the effect-pattern workspace and tail-calls the shared transfer primitive.
It does not perform shooting logic.
The routine builds collision lists and invokes player, weapon, terrain, special-attack, and platform collision passes.
It is called by the general gameplay update loop and is not owned by one boss.
The routine scans the complete object pool and classifies entries into five lists according to collision flags.
Several lists are consumed by player weapons, moving platforms, and targeting code, not only enemy logic.
The outer loop scans four entries in the alternating weapon-effect pool at FFBFC0/FFC020.
On overlap it subtracts projectile damage from target health and handles target defeat or hit scoring.
The fixed collision box is derived from the player object at FFA400.
The routine scans the primary hostile list and applies resource damage and response state to the player.
The routine constructs a collision box around the dedicated object at FFC5C0 and tests two target lists.
That object is initialized by player dash, projectile, and Z-Leo impact code; the routine performs no OAM writes.
The routine walks only the collision list selected by object flag bit 5.
Each entry dispatches one of three player-to-moving-platform contact handlers.
The dispatcher selects a contact handler using the object's mode field at offset 0x46.
The handlers place the player on a platform top or underside and are not limited to a ship.
After bounds checks the routine places the player at object Y minus 0x20 and links horizontal displacement.
No ship-specific state or data is accessed.
The routine clamps the player to object Y minus 0x20 for either vertical travel direction.
It is selected from the generic platform handler table and contains no Z-Leo-specific reference.
After overlap tests the routine places the player at object Y plus 0x20 and sets underside-contact flags.
It initializes neither a stage nor an enemy.
The routine subtracts one BCD unit from the two-byte counter at FFFF42 and saturates underflow at 9999.
It never accesses the four-byte score value at FFA212.
The routine updates an existing projectile trajectory and selects between shared impact-frame tables.
It writes no object type and performs no type-A4 initialization.
The routine calls the table initializer for the object already supplied in a0 and then writes type A4.
It performs no pool scan or free-slot test.
The routine advances the current animation frame and merges global stage bits into sprite attributes.
It neither consumes an initialization table nor allocates a projectile.
The routine adds 0x8000 to the vertical velocity field.
The engine's paired entry point subtracts velocity for upward acceleration before falling through here.
This branch is reached only when the animation script reads a negative end marker.
It writes the hidden display state and contains no boss-specific behavior.
The routine reads generic frame records through the pointer stored at object offset 0x54.
At the end marker it restores velocities and jumps through the callback stored at offset 0x48.
The entry copies a5 to a0 and falls directly into the type-88 projectile initializer.
Its callers therefore initialize the current object rather than merely retrieving an address.
The entry copies a5 to a0 and falls into code that writes object type 188 and shared effect graphics.
No seeking-missile address is stored or returned separately.
The entry copies a5 to a0 and falls through to the type-1A8 initializer.
Its observable behavior is projectile initialization, not a register-copy wrapper.
The first write assigns object type 0x1A8.
The value 0x2A does not occur in the routine.
The entry copies a5 to a0 and falls through to code that writes object type 160 and graphics attributes.
It initializes the current object rather than storing an object pointer.
The routine masks and merges word FF8092 into the sprite attribute field at offset 0x0E.
It reads neither an angle nor either velocity field.
The routine tests the object's RAM-slot bit and frame parity, then sets or clears bit 7 of display state.
It performs no trigonometry and never accesses a velocity field.
The entry copies a5 to a0 and falls into debris initialization with randomized velocity.
Its effect extends beyond register forwarding.
The routine loads object graphics metadata and writes a terminated pattern into the terrain tile map.
It contains no visibility test and never clears or destroys the object.
The routine indexes a two-entry handler table using the object's state field and jumps to the selected handler.
It does not read coordinates or compare screen bounds.
The routine initializes a fixed 0x24-frame destruction delay and then falls into its updater.
It performs no offscreen test.
This state decrements the existing delay and converts the object to its terminal effect type at expiry.
The destruction state was initialized by the preceding entry point; this code is its updater.
The routine derives a muzzle position from direction-indexed offsets and the current object coordinates.
It dispatches through a table containing the beam, bullet, homing, spread, and circular weapon handlers.
It does not construct sprite pieces or write the sprite output buffer.
The routine uses the current weapon index to select one entry from the adjacent fire-handler table.
It performs an indirect jump and contains no ammo or effect-visibility test.
The routine writes the object type, display state, and two object-state bytes.
It neither advances an animation nor assigns an animation frame table.
The routine tests one object-state flag and compares the animation counter at offset 0x0C with 0x80.
Either terminal condition sets the same inactive-object bit used by the surrounding removal handlers.
It does not read a health or damage field and contains no enemy-specific reference.
The object dispatch table invokes this routine as a recurring update handler.
Its state flags select initial motion, lifetime countdown, or impact initialization for the existing object.
It does not allocate a new object slot.
The routine only sets bit 4 of the object display-state word.
The same write terminates objects throughout the adjacent projectile and effect handlers; no priority field is calculated.
The only comparison uses the animation counter at object offset 0x0C and the terminal value 0x80.
At the terminal frame it replaces the display-state word with the hidden state 0x1000.
No damage or health field is read.
State flags choose between updating the current particle animation and attempting to allocate a child effect.
Both paths finish by marking the current object inactive, so spawning is only one state of the handler.
The entry fixes a0 to the shared object-pool base and d7 to 0x10 before entering the common clearing loop.
The common loop clears exactly 96 bytes per DBF iteration, so this entry clears 17 object-sized blocks rather than an arbitrary memory block.
Each loop iteration contains 24 longword stores and therefore clears one 96-byte object block.
The three adjacent entry points supply the shared object-pool base and counts of 8, 16, or 17 blocks.
The routine always fixes its destination to the wave output buffer at FFFF9800.
Its DBF counter starts at 0x50, so it clears 81 longwords rather than the 80 claimed by the generated comment.
The destination is fixed to the 512-byte tile-interpolation workspace at FF9800.
Both callers immediately generate interpolated tile data into that workspace.
The routine reads transition tables and writes the FF9600, FF9800, FF9A00, and FF9B00 RAM workspaces.
It neither accesses the VDP ports nor writes palette RAM; later code consumes the generated buffers.
The routine clears 24 longwords beginning at FF9400 and resets the transition progress counter.
It does not access either palette RAM or a palette data table.
The routine writes a fixed arrangement of zero and 0xE nibble masks into the FF9400 pattern buffer.
It then queues the buffer-related VDP register setup but does not update a position or scroll accumulator.
The routine selects two masks from a progress-indexed table and applies them to three rows of the transition pattern buffer.
It does not reset the object state or the transition progress value.
The routine loads the player object at FFA400 and returns the absolute horizontal delta in d0.
It returns the signed vertical delta in d2 and the constant 1 in d3; no norm, square, or root is calculated.
The routine starts at Entity_ObjectPool and clears consecutive 96-byte records through address DCA0.
Frontend and cutscene callers use the same routine, so the storage is neither boss-specific nor a separate boss buffer.
The routine scans 96-byte object records between bounds supplied by the caller and tests bit 6 of each record's state byte.
It returns a qualifying slot and status; it accesses neither palette data nor a VDP port.
The routine performs an unrolled scan of object records and returns when their type word is zero.
Each probe advances a0 by the 0x60-byte object stride; no position, velocity, or angle field is updated.
The routine invokes LZSSDecomp with the destination already configured in a2.
It performs no VDP-port access or DMA setup, so the destination is not necessarily VRAM.
The routine decodes blocks into the FFB400 staging buffer and passes each block to Gfx_ExecuteDMATransfer.
It waits for transfer completion before decoding the next block, establishing the staged VRAM behavior omitted by the previous name.
The routine indexes its table with StageTableIndex divided by two.
The table encodes decimal stages 1 through 50 in packed BCD and the results renderer consumes the stored byte as two digits.
After checking the frame-processing flag, the routine initializes word_FFF758 to ED00.
Sys_UpdateObjectCount derives the visible-object count from that cursor; this routine performs no VDP access.
The routine computes camera deltas, iterates the active visible-object list, and applies shared motion biases to object positions.
It also clamps player and object coordinates, so its behavior is object motion rather than a graphics-only scroll update.
The shared camera-motion routine passes each active object in a5 to this helper.
It clamps horizontal and vertical coordinates according to global bound-enable bits without testing any projectile identity or type.
The routine writes four-word sprite descriptors sequentially into the FFA100 display-list buffer.
It terminates the list with FFFF and tail-calls Sprite_AddToOAMBuffer; no entity velocity or friction value is read or updated.
Its secondary entry is called directly by UI_RenderDebugMenu, confirming UI ownership.
The block contains one subsystem call, to UI_BuildHUDSpriteList.
It performs no motion, collision, acceleration, or entity-state operation before continuing to Player_Update.
The routine calls the HUD sprite-list builder and HUD renderer, then indexes the Xi Tiger cutscene state table.
It invokes no physics, terrain, collision, or movement routine.
